text: At birth and for the first few weeks of life, a calf's rumen, reticulum, and omasum are undeveloped; the abomasum is the largest stomach compartment at this stage, and since the rumen is non-functional, milk passes directly into the abomasum. As long as the calf feeds only on milk, the rumen stays undeveloped. Once calves start eating grain and forage, a microbial population establishes itself in the rumen and reticulum, and those compartments begin to develop.
